meta.title: K-Bap — read any Korean menu
meta.description: Point your camera at a Korean menu. K-Bap translates every dish and marks the ones containing ingredients you listed as off-limits.
hero.sub: Point your camera at a Korean menu. Dishes you should skip come back marked.
hero.shotAlt: The K-Bap home screen, with a scan button and dishes rated safe for the user
features.title: What the app does
f1.title: Scan a menu
f1.body: One photo, and every dish comes back in your language.
f1.alt: The Scan a menu button on the K-Bap home screen
f2.title: A rating built from your list
f2.body: Four labels worked out from the list you saved. No data never means safe.
f2.alt: An ingredient panel listing butter as one to avoid, found in about 60 percent of restaurants
f3.title: 81 ingredients
f3.body: Tap what you skip, from peanut and butter to alcohol and shellfish.
f3.alt: A grid of ingredient chips with egg, butter and peanut selected
f4.title: Diet and religion presets
f4.body: Fifteen presets, among them vegan, halal, kosher and gluten-free, fill the list in.
f5.title: Ask in Korean without speaking it
f5.body: K-Bap writes your question, or the whole order, in Korean for the staff.
f5.alt: A Korean order card that asks for one dish and lists the ingredients the diner can't eat
f6.title: Browse without scanning
f6.body: Search dishes by name or scroll the catalog, rated the same way.
f6.alt: A grid of Korean dishes, each with a risk badge in the corner
f7.title: Reviews from other diners
f7.body: Read what other people made of a dish, and add your own once you've tried it.
f8.title: My Foods
f8.body: What you ordered and what you scanned, both kept on your profile.
